description:
Bloom Baby Classes' Caterpillar Club runs every Monday morning at Little Roo, 6 Temple Road, Blackrock, Co. Dublin, from 10am to 11am. It's designed for younger babies from around 6 weeks old up until they begin walking confidently (roughly 15 months), and is parent-accompanied throughout.

Each session blends original music, gentle sensory play and bonding activities, with new themes running through six-week terms across the year. The pace is kept calm and multi-sensory, suited to babies still finding their feet rather than mobile toddlers.

Pricing varies by term and is confirmed at the time of booking rather than published as a fixed rate, so check with the provider directly for the current term's cost.

Bloom Baby Classes brings its Midlands programme to Mucklagh, Co. Offaly, with age-graded sessions running from tiny newborns right through to four-year-olds. Caterpillar Club welcomes babies from birth to 6 months, using bright bespoke props and a different weekly theme, finishing each class with a gentle baby massage to settle baby for a nap.

Once babies are on the move, Busy Bees (6 months to walking, or around 15 months) introduces heuristic treasure baskets and more textured props, while building early social skills alongside other Bloom babies. Toddlers then move on to Bloom's own back-to-back music programme, including phonics and numbers songs, aimed at first learning goals.

Classes run on various days and times - see the provider's website for the current Mucklagh schedule. Pricing starts from €15 per class.

In Edgeworthstown, Co. Longford (Aghafin, Granard Rd), Bloom Baby Classes runs its full Midlands age range, from newborns up to four-year-olds, with separate class tiers for each stage of development. The youngest babies start in Caterpillar Club (0-6 months), exploring bright, bespoke props with a new theme each week and ending every session with a calming baby massage.

From around 6 months to walking (up to about 15 months), babies graduate to Busy Bees, where heuristic treasure baskets and sensory props encourage exploration and early social bonding with other babies. Older toddlers join Bloom's toddler classes, built around original music - including phonics and numbers songs - to support first learning goals.

Class days and times vary and are listed on the provider's website; classes cost from €15 each.

Bloom Baby Classes' Athlone base, on the Ballymahon Road in Cloghanboy, Co. Westmeath, runs the full Midlands programme spanning newborn to four years old. Babies begin in Caterpillar Club (0-6 months), where a different theme each week and a set of bright, bespoke props keep sessions fresh, closing with a soothing baby massage.

Busy Bees follows for babies from around 6 months until they're confidently walking (roughly 15 months), introducing treasure baskets and social play with other Bloom babies. Toddlers then move into Bloom's own toddler classes, set to original music including a phonics song and a calming zen track, aimed at early learning milestones.

Check the website for current Athlone class days, times and availability; sessions cost from €15.

Mullingar families can find Bloom Baby Classes' Midlands programme at Springfield (Spittlefield), Co. Westmeath, catering for babies and toddlers from birth right through to four years old. The entry-level Caterpillar Club (0-6 months) uses bright, bespoke props with a weekly changing theme, and every class ends with a gentle baby massage to wind down.

As babies near walking age (roughly 6 to 15 months), they move up to Busy Bees, exploring heuristic treasure baskets and building social connections with other Bloom babies. Toddlers continue on to Bloom's toddler classes, featuring original music - phonics, numbers and a calming zen track - designed around first learning goals.

Days and times vary by term and are posted on the provider's website; classes start from €15 each.

Baby Sensory runs its Glasnevin classes off Ballymun Road, Dublin, offering an educational and interactive developmental programme for babies aged 0 to 12 months (with separate 0-6 month and 6-12 month groupings). Sessions are built around each baby's natural play-rest-play cycle, so little ones are never overstimulated.

Classes run during school term time, with the venue and timetable for Glasnevin published on the Baby Sensory website - places are booked by term rather than as single drop-ins, starting from €17.75 per class. Beyond the sensory activities themselves, it's a good way for parents to meet others locally, swap questions and share early-parenthood experiences.

In Dublin 3, Baby Sensory holds its baby development classes on Howth Road, welcoming babies from 0-6 months and 6-12 months into separate age-appropriate groups. The programme is educational and interactive, structured around each baby's own play-rest-play rhythm to keep sessions calm rather than overwhelming.

Term-time classes here run alongside Baby Sensory's other Dublin venues, with days and times confirmed on the website; a term booking is required, and classes start from €17.75. Parents attending also get a regular chance to meet others nearby and swap notes on early baby life.

Baby Sensory's Stoneybatter classes run from 45a Ben Edair Road, Dublin 7, with separate groups for babies aged 0-6 months and 6-12 months. Each session is built around babies' natural play-rest-play cycle, using sensory activities designed to support learning without overstimulating them.

Classes run through the school term, and this Dublin 7 venue's schedule is listed on the Baby Sensory website; a term booking is required, with prices from €17.75 per class. It's also a handy way for local parents to connect, ask questions and share the ups and downs of the baby stage.

Baby Sensory holds classes in Raheny/Kilbarrack on Greendale Road, catering separately for babies aged 0-6 months and those 6-12 months old. The interactive programme follows each baby's play-rest-play cycle, giving structure to the sensory play without tipping into overstimulation.

Sessions run during school term time; check the Baby Sensory website for this venue's current days and times. A term booking is needed rather than single drop-ins, with classes priced from €17.75. Many parents also value it as a regular meet-up point with others in the Raheny and Kilbarrack area.

In Swords, Baby Sensory runs its classes on Feltrim Road, Drinan, with age-specific groups for babies 0-6 months and 6-12 months. The educational programme is timed around babies' natural play-rest-play pattern, so activities stay engaging without overstimulating them.

Classes follow the school term calendar, with the Swords timetable published on the Baby Sensory website; booking is by term, starting from €17.75 per class. As with Baby Sensory's other Dublin venues, it doubles as a friendly space for parents to meet, chat and share early parenting experiences.

Fingal Sports Office runs a free Parent and Toddler Movement Class at Baldoyle Community Centre every Thursday at 10am during term time, as part of a wider programme also covering Balbriggan, Swords, Lusk and Meakstown. It's aimed at babies who are walking, up to about 3-4 years old, and uses exercise, yoga and games to support movement development.

The Baldoyle/Howth session operates on a drop-in basis, but registration is required in advance - check Fingal Sports Office's social media for details. Classes generally follow the school calendar, though restart dates after holidays don't always line up exactly with term time, so it's worth checking before heading along.

The class is free to attend. For registration or queries, contact sports@fingal.ie.

Balbriggan Combined Club hosts a free Parent and Toddler Movement Class every Thursday at 9.30am during term time, run by Fingal Sports Office as part of a county-wide programme that also covers Swords, Baldoyle, Lusk and Meakstown. It suits toddlers who are walking, up to roughly 3-4 years old, with movement, yoga and games-based activities.

Sessions run on a drop-in basis but require advance registration via Fingal Sports Office's social media channels. The programme mostly follows school term dates, though it's worth checking socials after holidays, as the restart doesn't always match exactly.

There's no charge to attend. To register or for more information, contact sports@fingal.ie.

At Holywell Community Centre in Swords, Fingal Sports Office runs a free Parent and Toddler Movement Class every Tuesday at 9.15am during term time (Swords also has a second group at Applewood Community Centre on Tuesdays at 10.30am). The class is suitable for toddlers who are walking, up to about 3-4 years old, combining exercise, yoga and games for early movement development.

It's a drop-in session, though registration ahead of time is required - keep an eye on Fingal Sports Office's social media for updates, including when classes resume after school holidays, which doesn't always match term dates exactly.

Attendance is free. Contact sports@fingal.ie to register or ask questions.

St Macullin's Centre, Lusk Parish Hall, hosts a free Parent and Toddler Movement Class every Friday at 9.15am during term time, run by Fingal Sports Office alongside sister groups in Balbriggan, Swords, Baldoyle and Meakstown. It's designed for toddlers who are walking, up to roughly 3-4 years old, using movement, yoga and games to encourage development through exercise.

The Lusk group operates on a drop-in basis but does require advance registration - check Fingal Sports Office's social media for how to sign up and for updates on when the group restarts after school holidays.

There is no cost to attend. For registration or more information, contact sports@fingal.ie.

Meakstown Community Centre runs a free Parent and Toddler Movement Class every Tuesday at 10am during term time, delivered by Fingal Sports Office as part of a programme that also serves Balbriggan, Swords, Baldoyle and Lusk. The class suits toddlers who are walking, up to about 3-4 years old, using exercise, yoga and games to support early movement skills.

Classes are drop-in but require registering in advance through Fingal Sports Office's social media channels. Restart dates after school holidays are announced on socials too, since they don't always align precisely with term time.

The class is free. Contact sports@fingal.ie to register or find out more.

Louth's public libraries run a series of free Parent, Baby and Toddler groups, with the flagship session at Drogheda Library on Stockwell Lane every Thursday, 10am-12pm during term time (phone 041-9876162). It's a relaxed space with toys and noisy books, giving toddlers a first introduction to the library and parents, guardians and childminders a chance to meet others locally.

Drogheda Library also runs a Baby Book Club on the first Tuesday of the month at 10.30am (term time, no booking needed) - a morning of songs and stories for babies and their grown-ups. Over in Dundalk, the library on Roden Place runs its own Parent and Toddler Group on Thursdays, 10am-12pm, plus a Baby Book Club on the first Wednesday of the month at 10.30am (both free, no booking required; suitable for children under 4; contact 042-9353190 or libraryhelpdesk@louthcoco.ie).

All sessions are free to attend.

Families around Dunleer can access Louth County Council's free library-based Parent, Baby and Toddler groups in nearby Drogheda and Dundalk. Drogheda Library, Stockwell Lane, runs a Parent and Toddler Group every Thursday from 10am to 12pm during term time (041-9876162), with toys and books to explore, plus a monthly Baby Book Club - usually the first Tuesday at 10.30am - for songs and stories, no booking needed.

Dundalk Library and Library HQ on Roden Place offers a matching Parent and Toddler Group on Thursdays, 10am-12pm, and its own Baby Book Club on the first Wednesday of the month at 10.30am; both are open to all, with no booking required (children must be supervised, suitable for under-4s). Contact 042-9353190 or libraryhelpdesk@louthcoco.ie.

Every session listed is free of charge.

For families near Carlingford, the closest free library toddler groups run through Louth County Council in Drogheda and Dundalk. Drogheda Library on Stockwell Lane hosts a Parent and Toddler Group every Thursday, 10am-12pm during term time, with toys and noisy books for little ones and a chance for parents and childminders to connect (call 041-9876162); a Baby Book Club follows on the first Tuesday of the month at 10.30am.

Dundalk Library and Library HQ, Roden Place, runs its own Thursday Parent and Toddler Group (10am-12pm) alongside a first-Wednesday-of-the-month Baby Book Club at 10.30am. Both are drop-in, free, and suitable for children under 4 with adult supervision; reach the library on 042-9353190 or libraryhelpdesk@louthcoco.ie.

No booking or fee is required for any of these sessions.

Louth's libraries run several free Parent, Baby and Toddler sessions across the county. In Drogheda, the library on Stockwell Lane hosts a Parent and Toddler Group every Thursday, 10am-12pm (term time, 041-9876162), plus a Baby Book Club on the first Tuesday of the month at 10.30am for stories and songs.

Dundalk Library and Library HQ, Roden Place, mirrors this with a Thursday Parent and Toddler Group (10am-12pm) and a first-Wednesday Baby Book Club at 10.30am, both free and open without booking, suitable for children under 4 (contact 042-9353190 or libraryhelpdesk@louthcoco.ie).

All groups are free to attend and run during the school term.

Dundalk Library and Library HQ, Roden Place, runs a free Parent and Toddler Group every Thursday from 10am to 12pm during term time, with toys, books and plenty of company for both children and the adults minding them - no booking required, though children must be supervised throughout (suitable for under-4s). A Baby Book Club follows on the first Wednesday of the month at 10.30am, with library members able to borrow the featured book on the day. Contact 042-9353190 or libraryhelpdesk@louthcoco.ie.

Louth County Council runs a matching pair of sessions at Drogheda Library, Stockwell Lane - a Thursday Parent and Toddler Group (10am-12pm) and a first-Tuesday Baby Book Club at 10.30am (041-9876162).

Every session across both libraries is free.

The Brickx Club runs its brick-building and STEM sessions at a school/community venue in Knocklyon, Dublin, for children aged 3 to 12. The programme covers pre-school clubs, after-school clubs and Saturday workshops using creative, LEGO-based building to introduce STEM concepts through play.

As with Brickx Club's other South Dublin locations (Rathfarnham, Firhouse, Tallaght and Templeogue), specific days, times and pricing for the Knocklyon venue are set by the individual school or venue and aren't centrally published, so it's best to check directly. Parties, and Easter, summer and midterm camps, are also offered.

Requirements around parental attendance vary depending on the child's age and the specific class.

In Rathfarnham, The Brickx Club offers its LEGO-based brick-building and STEM club for children aged 3 to 12, running as part of a wider school-term programme across South Dublin. Sessions come in pre-school, after-school and Saturday workshop formats, all built around hands-on creative construction.

Day, time and pricing details for the Rathfarnham venue are set locally by the school or community centre hosting it rather than published centrally, so it's worth confirming directly before booking. The club also runs parties and camps over Easter, summer and midterm breaks at its various venues, which include Knocklyon, Firhouse, Tallaght and Templeogue.

Whether parents need to stay depends on the age group and class type booked.

The Brickx Club's Firhouse sessions bring LEGO-based brick-building and STEM activities to children aged 3 to 12, part of a school-term programme running at venues across Knocklyon, Rathfarnham, Tallaght and Templeogue as well. Formats include pre-school clubs, after-school clubs and Saturday workshops, all centred on creative, hands-on building.

Specific scheduling and pricing for the Firhouse venue are managed by the hosting school or community space rather than listed centrally, so check with the club directly for current details. Beyond term-time clubs, Brickx also runs parties and Easter, summer and midterm camps.

Parental attendance requirements vary by age group and class.

Children aged 3 to 12 in Tallaght can join The Brickx Club's brick-building and STEM sessions, run as pre-school clubs, after-school clubs or Saturday workshops depending on age. It's one of several South Dublin venues for the club, alongside Knocklyon, Rathfarnham, Firhouse and Templeogue.

As with the club's other locations, the exact day, time and price for the Tallaght sessions are set by the individual school or venue rather than published centrally - best to confirm directly. The club also runs popular parties and camps over the Easter, summer and midterm breaks.

Whether a parent needs to stay for the session depends on the child's age and class type.

The Brickx Club runs its Templeogue sessions for children aged 3 to 12, offering LEGO-based STEM activities as pre-school clubs, after-school clubs and Saturday workshops. It's part of a wider South Dublin programme that also covers Knocklyon, Rathfarnham, Firhouse and Tallaght.

Day, time and pricing information for the Templeogue venue is set by the hosting school or community venue rather than published centrally, so it's worth checking directly before signing up. Easter, summer and midterm camps, plus parties, round out the club's offering.

Parental attendance requirements vary depending on the age and class booked.

Olympian Gymnastics runs recreational gymnastics classes for children at Wesley College in Ballinteer, Dublin 16, on a drop-off basis. The club is registered with the Dun Laoghaire-Rathdown Sports Partnership club directory, which lists it among the area's community sports options.

Age groups, exact schedule and pricing for the Ballinteer venue weren't published on the club directory listing, so these should be confirmed directly with the club before enrolling.

At Templeogue College on Templeville Road, Olympian Gymnastics offers non-competitive GymTOTS, GymKIDZ and GymTEENS classes covering a wide age span, from 3.5 up to 18 years old. It's a recreational, non-competitive programme suited to beginners as well as more experienced young gymnasts.

Specific class days, times and pricing for the Templeogue venue weren't listed centrally, so it's best to check directly with the club for the current timetable and fees.

Olympian Gymnastics' Rathgar classes run at Danum on Zion Road, offering non-competitive GymKIDZ and GymTEENS sessions split into an under-12s group and a 13-17s group. The recreational format focuses on building gymnastics skills and confidence rather than competition.

Days, times and pricing for the Rathgar venue weren't published centrally and should be confirmed directly with the club.

On Milltown Road, Dublin 6, Olympian Gymnastics runs non-competitive GymKIDZ and GymTEENS classes, with separate groups for under-12s and 13-17 year olds. As with the club's other Dublin venues, the emphasis is on recreational gymnastics rather than competitive training.

Class schedule and pricing details for the Milltown venue weren't published centrally, so it's worth checking directly with the club before booking.

Olympian Gymnastics' Nutgrove venue, at the Nutgrove Shopping Centre in Rathfarnham, runs the club's full recreational range - GymTOTS, GymKIDZ and GymTEENS - catering for children and teens from as young as 18 months up to 16 years old, the broadest age span of the club's Dublin locations.

Specific days, times and pricing for the Nutgrove classes weren't published centrally and should be confirmed directly with the club.

Happy Cubs runs its Swim Cubs and Music Cubs sessions in Blackrock, Dublin, part of a wider network of baby, toddler and preschooler classes across Dublin, Wicklow and Cork. Swim Cubs focuses on water safety, basic swim technique and building confidence in the pool, while Music Cubs (roughly 3-6 months up to 5-6 years) explores rhythm, sound and social connection through songs and play.

Both class types are designed to develop life skills at each child's own pace, through play rather than pressure, and give parents a relaxed way to bond with their little one. Whether it's splashing about or singing along, the Blackrock sessions are one of several Happy Cubs venues in the area.

In Cherrywood, Dublin, Happy Cubs offers its Swim Cubs and Music Cubs classes for babies, toddlers and preschoolers as part of its Dublin, Wicklow and Cork network. Swim Cubs teaches water safety and basic swim technique in a confidence-building way, while Music Cubs welcomes children from around 3-6 months up to 5-6 years to explore rhythm and sound together.

Sessions are built around play, songs and each child's own pace of development, giving families a fun way to bond. Cherrywood is one of several Happy Cubs locations, alongside venues in Blackrock, Kilmainham, Loughlinstown and Sandymount.

Happy Cubs' Kilmainham classes bring both Swim Cubs and Music Cubs to babies, toddlers and preschoolers in this part of Dublin. Swim Cubs builds water confidence and basic swim technique, while Music Cubs (from roughly 3-6 months to 5-6 years) introduces rhythm, sound and social play through songs.

As with Happy Cubs' other Dublin, Wicklow and Cork venues, the focus is on developing life skills at a child's own pace, through play and plenty of smiles, giving parents a relaxed way to spend time with their little one.

In Loughlinstown, Happy Cubs runs its Swim Cubs and Music Cubs programme for babies, toddlers and preschoolers, part of a wider set of classes across Dublin, Wicklow and Cork. Swim Cubs covers water safety and basic swim technique in a confidence-building way, while Music Cubs (roughly 3-6 months to 5-6 years) is built around rhythm, songs and social connection.

Both class types lean on play rather than pressure, letting each child develop at their own pace while giving parents a lovely way to bond. Loughlinstown joins Blackrock, Cherrywood, Kilmainham and Sandymount among Happy Cubs' Dublin venues.

Happy Cubs' Sandymount classes offer both Swim Cubs and Music Cubs for babies, toddlers and preschoolers in the area. Swim Cubs teaches basic swim technique and water safety while building confidence in the pool, and Music Cubs (roughly 3-6 months up to 5-6 years) gives younger children a chance to explore rhythm, sound and social connection through play and songs.

As across Happy Cubs' other Dublin, Wicklow and Cork locations, sessions are designed around each child's own pace of development, making it an easy way for families to bond, whether your child is ready to splash or just loves to sing and move.

PlayAct Drama School's Inchicore branch offers dynamic, creative drama workshops where kids and teens can build confidence, express themselves and make new friends. Sessions combine acting, writing and prop-making, helping students develop social and communication skills in a relaxed, fun setting.

Classes are shaped around each student's own interests and strengths rather than a fixed curriculum, so the focus stays on adventure, discovery and learning through play as much as performance technique.

In Terenure, PlayAct Drama School runs creative drama workshops for kids and teens, built around acting, writing and prop-making to help students build confidence and express themselves. The relaxed, playful format is as much about making friends and developing communication skills as it is about performance.

Workshops meet students where they are, drawing on each child's interests and strengths to encourage exploration and creativity rather than following a rigid script.

PlayAct Drama School's Sandymount classes bring dynamic drama workshops to local kids and teens, mixing acting, writing and prop-making in a way that builds confidence and social skills alongside creativity. The tone stays fun and relaxed rather than performance-pressured.

As with PlayAct's other Dublin branches, sessions are tailored to each student's interests and strengths, with an emphasis on adventure, discovery and learning through play.

In Dun Laoghaire, PlayAct Drama School offers creative drama workshops for kids and teens, combining acting, writing and prop-making to help students grow in confidence and communication. The relaxed, playful approach makes it as much a place to make friends as to learn stagecraft.

Classes are built around each student's own interests and strengths, keeping the focus on discovery and learning through play rather than formal technique.

PlayAct Drama School runs junior drama classes for 5 to 7 year olds at Glasnevin Educate Together NS on Griffith Avenue, Dublin 11. Sessions combine acting, writing and prop-making in a relaxed, playful format designed to build confidence, communication and social skills at an early age.

This Glasnevin group focuses specifically on the youngest students, giving 5-7 year olds a gentle, age-appropriate introduction to drama before they might progress to PlayAct's other class levels.

Chime in & Play runs its parent-and-child music and play classes in Carlow, for children aged 1 to 5. Sessions are designed to build creativity, confidence and early friendships through playing and music together, while giving parents insight into their child's development along the way.

Classes and terms run at various times through the year, with some venues also offering a summer programme; check the website for the current Carlow schedule. Pricing starts from €15 per class, or from €50 for a full term.

At St Wolstan's Abbey in Celbridge, Co. Kildare, Chime in & Play offers parent-and-child music and play sessions for children aged 1 to 5. The classes combine playing and music to support development, while helping parents get to know their child's stage of growth and how to encourage it.

Days and times vary and are listed on the website, with some venues, including this one, running a summer term as well as the regular school-year programme. Classes start from €15, with terms from €50.

Chime in & Play's Wicklow classes run from the De La Salle Pastoral Centre on Saint Patrick's Road, offering parent-and-child music and play sessions for children aged 1 to 5. Through playing and music together, the classes aim to build creativity, confidence and early friendships for both children and parents.

Specific days and times are published on the website, and some terms run through the summer as well as during the school year. Pricing starts from €15 per class, or €50 for a full term.

In Bandon, Co. Cork, Chime in & Play runs parent-and-child music and play classes at South Main Street for children aged 1 to 5. Sessions blend music and play to support early development, while giving parents a chance to learn more about their child's stage and how to nurture it, all while having fun together.

Check the website for the current Bandon schedule, as days and times vary; some venues also run a summer term. Classes start from €15, with terms from €50.

Chime in & Play's Clonakilty classes run in Cloheen, Co. Cork, offering parent-and-child music and play sessions for children aged 1 to 5. The format is built around playing and music together, helping build creativity, confidence and friendships while giving parents insight into their child's development.

Days, times and term dates vary by venue and are listed on the website; some locations, potentially including Clonakilty, run a summer programme alongside the school-year terms. Pricing starts from €15 per class, or €50 for a full term.

Turtle Tots runs baby and toddler swimming lessons in Drogheda, Co. Louth, welcoming children from around 3 months up to 4.5 years old. The approach is child-centred throughout, with activities adapted to suit each child's stage and confidence in the water.

By the end of the baby programme, children have been introduced to all the individual techniques needed to build toward independent swimming, taught by trained teachers who keep sessions fun and sociable as well as focused on essential water-safety skills. Classes here start from €21.

In Dungarvan, Co. Waterford, Turtle Tots offers swimming lessons for babies and toddlers from around 3 months to 4.5 years old, with activities tailored to each child rather than a one-size-fits-all approach. The programme builds progressively, teaching the separate skills that lead toward independent swimming by the end of the baby stage.

Trained Turtle Tots teachers keep the Dungarvan sessions sociable and enjoyable while still covering essential life-saving skills. Classes start from €21.

Turtle Tots' Kilbarry classes bring child-centred swimming lessons to babies and toddlers in Waterford, catering for children from roughly 3 months up to 4.5 years. Each child's activities are adapted to their own needs and confidence level in the pool.

The programme is structured to teach all the separate skills needed for independent swimming by the end of the baby stage, delivered by trained teachers who balance fun and sociability with essential water-safety instruction. Prices start from €21 per class.

Families in Portlaoise, Co. Laois, can join Turtle Tots swimming lessons at Maryborough for babies and toddlers aged from around 3 months to 4.5 years old. Every session is nurtured around the individual child, with activities adjusted to suit their stage of development.

By the close of the baby programme, children have worked through all the separate techniques that build toward independent swimming, taught by trained instructors in a fun, sociable setting that still prioritises essential life-saving skills. Classes start from €21.

Turtle Tots runs swimming lessons at Knock, Limerick, for babies and toddlers from around 3 months up to 4.5 years old. The lessons are genuinely child-centred, with each child's activities adapted to their own needs and pace in the water.

Over the course of the baby programme, children are introduced to all the individual techniques required for independent swimming later on, guided by trained teachers who keep the atmosphere fun and sociable while still covering essential water-safety skills. Classes start from €21.

In Co. Monaghan, Turtle Tots offers child-centred swimming lessons for babies and toddlers from around 3 months up to 4.5 years old, with every activity nurtured and adapted to the individual child. By the end of the baby programme, children have built up all the separate skills and techniques that lead toward independent swimming.

Trained, skilled teachers keep the Monaghan sessions fun and sociable, while still focusing on essential life-saving skills for young swimmers. Classes start from €21.

Turtle Tots' Rathnaconeen classes bring child-centred swimming lessons to babies and toddlers across Co. Mayo, for children from roughly 3 months to 4.5 years old. Activities are adapted to each child individually rather than following a fixed programme.

By the end of the baby stage, children have covered all the separate techniques needed to build toward independent swimming, taught by trained instructors who balance fun and sociability with essential water-safety skills. Classes start from €21.

In Knockacroghery, Co. Mayo, Turtle Tots runs swimming lessons for babies and toddlers aged roughly 3 months to 4.5 years, with each child's activities nurtured and adapted to their own needs. The baby programme is designed to teach, step by step, all the individual techniques that lead toward independent swimming.

Trained, skilled teachers keep sessions sociable and enjoyable while still covering essential life-saving skills. Classes start from €21.

Turtle Tots' Quay Road classes in Co. Mayo offer child-centred swimming lessons for babies and toddlers from around 3 months to 4.5 years old. Every child's activities are adapted individually, with the baby programme building progressively toward the separate skills needed for independent swimming.

Trained instructors keep the sessions fun and sociable, while still prioritising essential water-safety skills for young swimmers. Classes start from €21.

In Ballincar, Co. Sligo, Turtle Tots runs swimming lessons for babies and toddlers from around 3 months up to 4.5 years old, with each child nurtured individually rather than taught to a fixed script. By the end of the baby programme, children have built up all the separate techniques and practices needed for independent swimming.

Trained, skilled teachers keep the Sligo sessions sociable and fun, while still teaching essential life-saving skills. Classes start from €21.

Drum Gospel Hall on Main Street hosts an unverified toddler group in Co. Monaghan, meeting every second Tuesday from 10am to 12pm during school term time. As it has no current social media presence or webpage, Tots Spots could not confirm whether it's still running - Monaghan Childcare Committee last listed it as active in September 2024. Contact Margaret on 086 352 5405 to check before attending.

It's one of several similarly unverified groups around the county, including sessions in Smithborough, Glaslough, Tyholland and Monaghan town - worth checking the Tots Spots map for other options nearby.

Tyholland Community Centre in Skinnagin, Co. Monaghan, is home to an unverified toddler group meeting every second Friday from 10am to 11.30am. With no social media presence or website to confirm current status, Tots Spots lists it based on Monaghan Childcare Committee records from September 2024 - contact Louise on 00 44 7821 554012 to check it's still running before you go.

It's one of a handful of similarly unverified groups across Co. Monaghan, including ones in Drum, Smithborough, Glaslough and Monaghan town; the Tots Spots map lists further options nearby.

Smithborough Presbyterian Church Hall runs an unverified toddler group called Junior Junction, meeting every Tuesday from 10.30am to 12pm. As with several other Monaghan groups, there's no current social media page or website to confirm it's still active - it was last listed as operating by Monaghan Childcare Committee in September 2024. Contact Carole on 087 243 6997 to check before attending.

Other unverified groups in the county run in Drum, Glaslough, Tyholland and Monaghan town; see the Tots Spots map for further local options.

Oakland Community Centre in Glaslough, Co. Monaghan, hosts an unverified toddler group every Tuesday from 9.30 to 11.30am during term time. It has no social media presence or webpage, so Tots Spots can't confirm current status - Monaghan Childcare Committee last recorded it as active in September 2024. Contact Claire on 083 038 0203 before heading along.

It joins a handful of similarly unverified groups across Monaghan, in Drum, Smithborough, Tyholland and Monaghan town; check the Tots Spots map for more options nearby.

St Patrick's Church Hall in Monaghan town runs an unverified toddler group every Thursday from 10.30am to 12pm during school term time. With no current social media presence or website, Tots Spots could not confirm whether it's still operating - Monaghan Childcare Committee last listed it as active in September 2024. Contact Gayle on 047 81136 to check before attending.

It's one of several similarly unverified groups across the county, also including sessions in Drum, Smithborough, Glaslough and Tyholland; see the Tots Spots map for further local listings.

Dublin School of Music's Terenure branch, at Eaton House on Terenure Road North, offers one-to-one instrumental and vocal lessons in piano, guitar, violin, voice, flute and drums for children and adults of all abilities. Tuition starts from €30 for a 30-minute lesson, with 45 and 60-minute slots also available, along with term bundles and sibling discounts. The Terenure branch runs six days a week, Monday to Saturday, on a weekly subscription basis.

At 20 Kilmacud Road Lower in Stillorgan, Dublin School of Music offers private one-to-one lessons in piano, guitar, violin, voice, flute and drums for students of all ages and abilities. Teaching is delivered by concert performers and examiners, with optional exam preparation for students working toward grades.

Lessons run on a weekly subscription, Monday through Saturday, starting from €30 for a 30-minute slot; 45 and 60-minute lessons are also available, along with term bundles and sibling discounts.

Dublin School of Music's Tallaght branch, at Old Bawn Shopping Centre, provides one-to-one instrumental and vocal tuition - piano, guitar, violin, voice, flute and drums - for children and adults at every level. Lessons are taught by concert performers and examiners, with exam preparation available for interested students.

This location runs seven days a week, including Sunday lessons not offered at all branches, on a weekly subscription basis. Tuition starts from €30 for a 30-minute lesson, with longer 45 and 60-minute slots, term bundles and sibling discounts also available.

Lessons incorporate improvisation, songwriting, audio engineering, music theory, ear training, composition and performance. Grade exam preparation (optional) is available for all instruments.

Artzone's Dundrum summer art camp runs at Taney Parish Centre, Taney Road, covering drawing, painting, craft and other visual arts activities for primary school children. Sessions are led by qualified art teachers and run from 10am to 1pm, Monday to Friday, over a full week.

Age-graded groups run concurrently at this venue: Junior Art Camp (5-6 years), Intermediate Art Camp (7-8 years) and Senior Art Camp (9-13 years), with children dropped off for the week. This particular week (20-24 July 2026) is one of three summer weeks offered here, with further weeks running 4-7 August and 10-14 August 2026, priced at €160 for the full week.

Artzone runs after-school art classes at St. Andrew's NS in Malahide on Wednesdays, split into a Junior group (roughly 5-7.5 years) and a Senior Primary group (about 6.5-12.5 years), covering drawing, painting and other craft activities suited to each age band.

Beyond the weekly term-time classes, Artzone also runs summer camps at this venue for children in the same broad 5-12.5 age range.

Artzone's Rathfarnham branch, based at VFI Court on Castleside Drive, runs art classes for children aged 5 to 12, covering drawing, painting and craft activities in a structured, small-group setting.

Soccer Stars runs football lessons for toddlers and young children aged 1.5 to just under 6 years old, with classes across Co. Wexford, Co. Wicklow, Co. Waterford and Co. Kilkenny.

Sessions introduce children to the basics of football in a pressure-free, age-appropriate way, giving them an early taste of the sport across several venues in the south-east.

The focus is on fun, friendly, non-competitive football that builds coordination, confidence and teamwork, with parents encouraged to join in alongside their children. Membership runs at €50 per month.

Soccer Stars' Templeogue class runs at Our Lady's School on Terenure Road every Sunday morning from 9am to 11.45am, for children aged 18 months to 8 years. Messy Adventures runs messy play sessions in Swords every Friday, with two slots at 9.30am and 11.15am, for babies and children aged roughly 6 months to 6 years. The sensory play format encourages fine and gross motor skill development, hand-eye coordination and independent exploration, alongside parent-and-child bonding time.

Classes are designed to be fully inclusive and welcoming to all babies and children. Messy Adventures also runs sessions in Malahide and Raheny, with pricing at €16 per messy play class (€14 for Role Play Village) and an automatic 30% sibling discount at checkout.

In Malahide, Messy Adventures runs two types of sessions weekly: Tuesday messy play at 11am, and Thursday Role Play Village Active sessions at 10am and 11.20am, for children aged roughly 6 months to 6 years. Messy Adventures brings its sensory messy play sessions to Phibblestown, Dublin, for babies and children aged roughly 6 months to 6 years. Sessions are fully inclusive and welcoming to all babies and children, priced at €16 per class with a 30% sibling discount applied automatically at checkout. Messy Adventures also has sessions in Malahide, Swords and Raheny.

Music Cubs runs parent-and-child music classes in Rathfarnham for babies, toddlers and older 'big cubs' aged 0 to 5 years. Each 30-minute session is packed with melody, play and simple percussion, introducing rhythm, beats and tempo alongside live performances on a range of instruments.

It's a gentle, fun way to nurture children's natural love of music together with a parent. Pricing runs from €52 for a 4-week term up to €65 for a 5-week term; Music Cubs also runs classes at other venues across Dublin.

At Terminus Mills on Bóthar Chluain Sceach in Rathmines, Music Cubs offers parent-and-child music sessions for children aged 0 to 5. Classes run 30 minutes, mixing live instrument performances with simple percussion, rhythm and melody, giving even the youngest babies a playful introduction to music.

Terms cost €52 for 4 weeks or €65 for 5 weeks. Music Cubs runs similar sessions at several other Dublin venues, including Rathfarnham and Dundrum.

Music Cubs' Dundrum classes offer 30-minute parent-and-child music sessions for babies, toddlers and older children up to age 5. Each class blends live instrument performances with simple percussion and rhythm games, building a playful, shared musical experience for parent and child.

A 4-week term costs €52, or €65 for 5 weeks. Dundrum is one of several Dublin locations where Music Cubs runs classes.

Music Cubs runs parent-and-child music classes across Dublin, including this D04 venue, for children aged 0 to 5 years. Sessions last 30 minutes and combine melody, play and simple percussion, with live performances on a variety of instruments to spark little ones' natural love of music.

Terms cost €52 for 4 weeks or €65 for 5 weeks.

Turtle Tots Dublin runs its Kilmainham swimming classes for babies and toddlers aged roughly 3 months to 4.5 years, with activities nurtured and adapted to each individual child rather than a fixed curriculum. Activities are adapted to each individual child, with the baby programme structured to teach, step by step, the separate skills needed for independent swimming.

Trained instructors keep the Finglas sessions sociable and fun, while still focusing on essential life-saving skills. Classes start from €21.

Dublin Stage School's Junior Stage School class runs at St. John's National School, Church Road, Killiney, for children aged 4 to 6. The class is Garda-vetted, drop-off, and capped at a maximum of 17 students. Fees are €19 per session (a monthly payment plan is available), with a two-week trial costing €35 - deducted from term fees if your child continues. Free parking is available at the venue.

Dublin Stage School's Blackrock branch offers acting, singing and dance classes for young performers aged 4 to 18, part of a group of schools that also includes Killiney and Castleknock. Professional coaching here focuses on building confidence and creativity in a supportive, safe environment.

Students from across Dublin Stage School have gone on to perform at venues such as the Bord Gáis Energy Theatre, the National Concert Hall and the Gaiety Theatre, and have featured in productions including Miss Saigon, Les Misérables, Matilda and Joseph and the Amazing Technicolor Dreamcoat, plus screen credits such as Vikings, Penny Dreadful and Angela's Ashes.

Me & You Music runs its playful introduction-to-music classes in Dun Laoghaire, suitable for children from around 4 months to 6 years old. Led by Mischa, sessions encourage children to sing, dance and explore, with fun kept firmly at the centre of every class.
